column1: # path-guard.tsv -- THE ONE HOME of the PreToolUse path-guard's deny-list
# (#707). Read at the point of use by hooks/pretooluse-path-guard.sh. NEVER
# copied into a second place or inlined into the hook script itself.
# Zach, 129 times over 3,944 typed messages: some form of "never hand-edit
# that file". Every one of those named a known path with a known front door
# that should have been used instead -- the argument for a guard over prose:
# the rule was already written down, and got said anyway.
# Columns:  pattern (TAB) front door
# `pattern` is a bash `case` glob matched against the tool call's absolute
# file_path. Order matters: FIRST MATCH WINS, so a more specific row (an
# exact installed path) must sit above a broader one (its directory's `*`).
# Every row must carry a real alternative. A row with no front door blocks
# with nowhere to go, which means the write it blocks was legitimate and the
# row itself is wrong -- do not add one.
# Two rows this table does NOT carry, because a path pattern alone cannot
# judge them without also knowing whose account or whose repo is asking:
# a copied bin/lib/labels.tsv (must not fire on hf7y/realisateur's own copy,
# the source) and a write into another self-dev account's project tree
# (must not fire on this account's own project). Both are decided in code in
# hooks/pretooluse-path-guard.sh, right beside this table, not duplicated
# into a second data file.
/usr/local/bin/gh
